topic.title: Memes only work when somebody else starts them
topic.claim: A brand that posts its own meme templates is asking you to laugh on cue, and that is why it fails.
topic.behaviour: Film teams and brands drop ready-made meme templates, then wait for people to use them. When a meme starts on its own, the brand jumps in within days with puns.
topic.mechanism: A meme feels funny because it came from the crowd. When the brand hands out the template, it shows the joke was planned and the crowd is staff.
topic.group: Instagram and X users who can smell a planned viral moment
topic.moment: You see a brand's post that says 'make your own memes' and you scroll on.

turn.believed: Brands go viral by being funny.
turn.actually: Brands go viral by arriving late to someone else's joke. Making the joke yourself rarely works.

topic.feeling: talked down to, like a target
topic.villain: the engagement metric that rewards brands for forcing a joke
topic.because: A social team is judged on reach, so they push templates. Real memes come free and the brand only borrows them.

proof.fact: The film's official X handle posted meme templates made from the trailer ahead of its November 5 release. Many users said memes are the wrong tool for a story people hold in reverence.

topic.payoff: If you need to hand people the template, it's an ad.
topic.send_to: The friend who works in social media and hates the 'make it viral' brief
real_details: Gowardhan posted a video about the ghee meme and Zomato joined in with Saif-themed puns on delivery bags
topic.news_peg: Ramayana makers' meme templates backlash, 26 October 2026, and the Saif ghee meme brand pile-on, 30 October 2026
topic.why_now: The film releases on 5 November and the ghee meme is the month's biggest.

score.why: A brand handing out meme templates is an ad. Brands go viral by arriving late to someone else's joke.

sources.fact: The Saif Ali Khan ghee meme began organically from his KBC reaction, with no brand campaign or template behind it. This partly supports the claim that organic memes work better than planted ones. It does not show a brand pile-on or a Ramayana template backlash.
sources.excerpt: Social media users began reacting to Saif’s expression. There was no elaborate campaign or planned product narrative. the internet didn't need much convincing.

sources.fact: Gowardhan Ghee joined the organic meme through a collaboration video with Saif Ali Khan, and ThePrint called it a marketing win. This contradicts the claim that brand involvement in a meme necessarily fails. I found no reported pile-on, and the page does not mention puns or the Ramayana templates.
sources.excerpt: And, after all the chatter, the collaboration of the year finally happened. in an Instagram video, Khan collaborated with the ghee brand urging fans to move past the ghee conversation. a case study in how a small moment can become a brand's biggest marketing win. For a brand, that kind of recall is a pretty sweet deal or, in this case, a very ghee-rich one.

cover.headline: A brand's meme template isn't a joke. It's [homework].
cover.sub: You scroll past it in a second and never ask why.

paragraphs:
When a brand hands you a meme template, it isn't sharing a joke. It's homework.
Swipe to read →
slides.why_swipe: Why does a template feel like homework?

paragraphs: Every big launch handle now drops the same post. A still from the trailer, blank space on top, and a chirpy "make your own memes!"
You feel the cringe and scroll on in a second. The top reply is usually some version of "admin, we see you," with more likes than the post.
slides.why_swipe: Has this actually backfired on someone big?

paragraphs: The Ramayana film's official X handle did this before its 5 November release.
Many people said memes were the wrong tool for a story they hold in reverence. Reverence made it sting. But the template was a plan, and it showed.
slides.why_swipe: Is it only big films that do this?

paragraphs: Same move, smaller stage. An OTT handle posts a blank still from its new show. A food app posts "caption this" with its logo in the corner.
Both wait for you to do the funny part.
slides.why_swipe: So what does a meme that works look like?

paragraphs: Now look at October's biggest meme. Saif Ali Khan's reaction on KBC turned into the ghee joke everyone was sharing.
Nobody planned it. There was no campaign and no template. The internet just ran with it.
slides.why_swipe: Did any brand win from it?

paragraphs: And the winning brand came in late. Gowardhan made a video with Saif once the chatter was everywhere.
That was planned too. But the crowd made the joke first. A brand pun on a trending meme lands for the same reason.
slides.why_swipe: Then why does the template fail?

paragraphs: A meme is funny because the crowd made it. A template makes you do the unpaid half of a campaign.
Brands still do it because social teams are judged on reach. The report counts posts, not cringe.
slides.why_swipe: What does that look like from inside the team?

paragraphs: Inside the social team, the brief reads the same every time: make it viral, keep it on brand, by Friday.
That's why the chirpy caption lands like a teacher's worksheet. It talks down to you, and counts your reply anyway.
A real meme is one you'd have made anyway, logo or no logo.
If you have to hand people the template, it was never a meme. It was an ad with a blank space for your face.

end.save: Read it again the next time a launch post asks you to make its memes.
end.send: Send to the friend in social media who just got another 'make it viral' brief.
end.promise: How brands really sell to us.

draft.alt_text: A ten-slide text post arguing that brand meme templates are homework, not jokes. It notes the Ramayana film's official X handle posting meme templates before release, which many said was wrong for a revered story, and says the reverence made it sting but the template itself was a visible plan. It points to typical templates like an OTT show's blank still or a food app's 'caption this' post. It contrasts these with the organic Saif Ali Khan ghee meme from KBC, which Gowardhan joined later with a planned video that worked because the crowd made the joke first. It says social teams are judged on reach, describes the typical 'make it viral' brief, and closes by saying a template you have to hand out is an ad with a blank space for your face.

claims.text: The Ramayana film's official X handle posted meme templates made from the trailer before its 5 November release.
Many people said memes were the wrong tool for a story they hold in reverence.
The Saif Ali Khan ghee meme began from his KBC reaction with no campaign or template behind it.
Gowardhan made a video with Saif Ali Khan after the chatter around the meme.
